## Example 4.11 {#iv4-example-4-11 .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson }

<p>Given the position vectors <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}=\overrightarrow{OA}=(1,3,4)"></span> and <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{b}=\overrightarrow{OB}=(-1,3,2)"></span></p><p><strong>a)</strong> Draw a diagram of the situation and express <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{e}=\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}"></span> in component form</p><p><strong>b)</strong> Find the unit vectors <span data-math="\widehat{\underset{\sim}{a}}"></span>, <span data-math="\widehat{\underset{\sim}{b}}"></span> and <span data-math="\widehat{\underset{\sim}{e}}"></span></p><div class="m-split"><div><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="m-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show diagram and (a)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div data-magnitude="example11"></div><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{e}=-2\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{k}"></span></div></div></div></div><div><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="m-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show (b)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\widehat{\underset{\sim}{a}}=\frac1{\sqrt{26}}\underset{\sim}{i}+\frac3{\sqrt{26}}\underset{\sim}{j}+\frac4{\sqrt{26}}\underset{\sim}{k}"></span></div><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\widehat{\underset{\sim}{b}}=-\frac1{\sqrt{14}}\underset{\sim}{i}+\frac3{\sqrt{14}}\underset{\sim}{j}+\frac2{\sqrt{14}}\underset{\sim}{k}"></span></div><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\widehat{\underset{\sim}{e}}=-\frac1{\sqrt2}\underset{\sim}{i}-\frac1{\sqrt2}\underset{\sim}{k}"></span></div></div></div></div></div>
<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 4.11 · p. 32</div>

::: notes
a) e=b−a=(-2,0,-2)=-2i−2k. b) |a|=sqrt(26), |b|=sqrt(14), |e|=sqrt(8)=2sqrt(2). All three displayed vectors have magnitude 1. The supporting 3D diagram shows a=OA, b=OB and e=AB; both points have y=3. Ask students to sketch before revealing the diagram.
:::
